work: Pagan Sources Quoted in the New Testament
attribution: A curated collection of Greek passages quoted or alluded to in the New Testament. Aratus follows the Perseus edition of the Phaenomena; the other passages follow the standard critical texts, with the New Testament quotations fixing the wording. Translations are the editor’s, in the public domain.

verses.text: From Zeus let us begin; him do we mortals never leave unspoken.
verses.greek: ἐκ Διὸς ἀρχώμεσθα, τὸν οὐδέποτʼ ἄνδρες ἐῶμεν

verses.text: Filled with Zeus are all the highways,
verses.greek: ἄρρητον· μεσταὶ δὲ Διὸς πᾶσαι μὲν ἀγυιαί,

verses.text: and all the marketplaces of men; filled too the sea
verses.greek: πᾶσαι δʼ ἀνθρώπων ἀγοραί, μεστὴ δὲ θάλασσα

verses.text: and the harbours; and in every way we all have need of Zeus.
verses.greek: καὶ λιμένες· πάντη δὲ Διὸς κεχρήμεθα πάντες.

verses.text: For we are also his offspring; and kindly to men he
verses.greek: τοῦ γάρ καὶ γένος εἰμέν· ὁ δʼ ἤπιος ἀνθρώποισιν

verses.text: For we are your offspring, and alone of all that live and move as mortals on the earth we bear the likeness of your voice.
verses.greek: ἐκ σοῦ γὰρ γένος ἐσμέν, ἤχου μίμημα λαχόντες μοῦνοι, ὅσα ζώει τε καὶ ἕρπει θνήτʼ ἐπὶ γαῖαν.

verses.text: Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons. (The words of Acts 17:28a, “in him we live and move and have our being,” are also traditionally ascribed to Epimenides’ Cretica.)
verses.greek: Κρῆτες ἀεὶ ψεῦσται, κακὰ θηρία, γαστέρες ἀργαί.
